title: Data Interpretation: Reading Tables and Charts
subject: math

sections.body: Data interpretation means answering questions from a table or chart. Read the title, the labels and the units first. Then read only the numbers the question needs.
Here is a made-up table of a shop's monthly sales (units sold): January 100, February 150, March 120, April 180. The data is invented for practice.

Change from one value to another: percent change = (new - old) ÷ old × 100. January to February: (150 - 100) ÷ 100 × 100 = 50% increase. February to March: (120 - 150) ÷ 150 × 100 = -20%, a 20% decrease.
Always divide by the OLD value. A rise from 50 to 60 is 20%. A fall from 60 to 50 is about 16.7%, a different percent, because the starting value is different.
In a pie chart, a slice's angle is its share of 360 degrees. A quarter of the data has an angle of 25% × 360 = 90 degrees.
Find a table in a newspaper or school book. Write three questions about it: one about a percent change, one about a total, one about the biggest change.
Ask 'what is this chart really showing?' before doing any sums. Check the units and the start of the axis. Invented data keeps this a maths exercise, not a claim about any real shop.

quiz.q: A shop sold 100 units in January and 150 units in February. What is the percent increase?
hints: The change is 150 - 100. The old value is the January figure.
Example: from 50 to 60 is a rise of 10, and 10 ÷ 50 × 100 = 20%. Use the same steps.

quiz.q: Sales were Jan 100, Feb 150, Mar 120, Apr 180. Which month had the biggest rise from the month before?
hints: Work out the change from the previous month for each month after the first.
Feb: +50. Mar: 120 - 150. Apr: 180 - 120. Which is largest?
Example: values 10, 14, 11, 20 → changes +4, -3, +9, so the last month had the biggest rise. Compare the changes here.
quiz.explain: February +50, March -30, April +60. April is the biggest rise.

quiz.q: Sales fell from 150 in February to 120 in March. What is the percent decrease?
hints: Find the fall in units, then divide by the old value.
The old value is the February figure. 150 - 120 is the fall.
Example: 200 falling to 150 is a fall of 50, and 50 ÷ 200 × 100 = 25%. Use 150 as the old value.
